nodes.title: SG-2.1 · Merge duplicate content loader/validator into one module
nodes.body:
Context: backend/game/src/content has two overlapping implementations of loadWorld and validateWorld. loader.ts returns scenes as an array and validates a LoadedWorld. world.ts returns scenes as a record and validates (WorldDef, SceneDef[]). It does field checks on load. tests/content.test.ts imports loader.ts and tests/validator.test.ts imports world.ts. Desired behavior: one module survives, all imports point to it, and the validator tests cover the surviving one. Expected result: no duplicate implementation remains and unknown scene, object, character and flag references are tested. Why: two diverging validators make content errors unreliable for the later AI development worker.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the repo after the change, when src/content is listed, then only one module exports loadWorld and validateWorld and src/content/world.ts no longer exists
- Given every file under backend/game/src and backend/game/tests, when imports are searched, then none reference content/world
- Given a world whose scene uses an unknown goto_scene target, say character, set_flag flag and discover object, when validateWorld runs, then it returns unknown scene, unknown character, unknown flag and unknown object errors
- Given the real the-boys-room content, when loadWorld and validateWorld run, then validateWorld returns an empty array


## Scope
- In scope: backend/game/src/content/loader.ts
- In scope: delete backend/game/src/content/world.ts
- In scope: backend/game/tests/validator.test.ts
- In scope: backend/game/tests/loader.test.ts
- Out of scope: Go backend
- Out of scope: engine, systems and state modules
- Out of scope: content YAML changes
- Preserve: content.test.ts behavior on the-boys-room
- Preserve: LoadedWorld.scenes remains an array of SceneDef
- Preserve: existing error message formats such as 'unknown scene: X'


## Technical constraints
- TypeScript with vitest and the yaml package; no new dependencies
- Surviving module path is backend/game/src/content/loader.ts


## Definition of done
- Only one loader/validator implementation exists
- npm test and npm run typecheck pass in backend/game


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Single loadWorld with strict field validation
nodes.body:
Context: loader.ts loadWorld casts YAML without checking fields, while world.ts checks string fields, mapping shape and scene id match. Desired behavior: the surviving loadWorld returns scenes as SceneDef[] and throws the stricter errors. Expected result: malformed world.yaml or scene files fail loudly in one place. Why: invalid content must be caught at load time.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a world.yaml missing the id string field, when loadWorld runs, then it throws an error mentioning 'id'
- Given world.yaml listing scene s2 with no scenes/s2.yaml, when loadWorld runs, then it throws an error mentioning s2.yaml
- Given scenes/s.yaml declaring id other, when loadWorld runs for scene s, then it throws an error mentioning 'expected s'
- Given valid files, when loadWorld runs, then scenes is an array containing the scene with id s


## Scope
- In scope: loadWorld in loader.ts
- Out of scope: validateWorld
- Preserve: LoadedWorld type with scenes: SceneDef[]


## Technical constraints
- No new dependencies


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- loadWorld enforces field checks and returns scenes as an array


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · One validator, world.ts removed, imports updated
nodes.body:
Context: validateWorld(world, scenes) in world.ts duplicates validateWorld(LoadedWorld) in loader.ts and is imported only by tests/validator.test.ts. Desired behavior: remove world.ts and test the loader.ts validator. Expected result: a single validator with tests for every reference kind. Why: avoids drift between two validators.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given src/content, when listed, then world.ts is absent
- Given the invalid fixture world, when validateWorld runs, then errors contain unknown scene: nowhere, unknown character: ghost, unknown flag: zzz and unknown object: nope
- Given the valid fixture world, when validateWorld runs, then it returns []
- Given the real the-boys-room content, when validated, then it returns []


## Scope
- In scope: delete world.ts
- In scope: validator.test.ts import and calls
- Out of scope: fixture content changes
- Preserve: content.test.ts tests


## Technical constraints
- Fixtures stay WorldDef plus SceneDef; tests compose them into a LoadedWorld


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- No file imports content/world
- Validator tests pass against loader.ts


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Port strict field validation into loader.ts loadWorld
nodes.body:
Context: loader.ts L10-L25 reads world.yaml and scenes with plain casts. Desired behavior: reuse world.ts helpers isRecord, requireString and requireStringArray and its scene id mismatch check. Expected result: loadWorld throws descriptive errors for malformed content and returns scenes as SceneDef[].

## Acceptance criteria
- loadWorld throws when world.yaml lacks a string id, title or startScene
- loadWorld throws naming the missing file, such as s2.yaml, when a listed scene file is absent
- loadWorld throws when a scene file's id differs from the listed id
- loadWorld returns LoadedWorld whose scenes is an array in world.yaml order


## Scope
- In scope: loader.ts loadWorld and helpers
- Out of scope: validateWorld
- Out of scope: tests
- Preserve: export names loadWorld, validateWorld, LoadedWorld


## Technical constraints
- Missing scene error message must still contain '<sceneId>.yaml'
- Code path: `backend/game/src/content/loader.ts`


## Dependencies
- REQ1


## Definition of done
- npm run typecheck passes in backend/game
- loadWorld on the-boys-room still succeeds


## Clarifying questions
- None
nodes.summary: Replace the unchecked cast in loader.ts loadWorld with world.ts's checked parsing, keeping scenes as an array.
nodes.description: Context: loader.ts L10-L25 reads world.yaml and scenes with plain casts. Desired behavior: reuse world.ts helpers isRecord, requireString and requireStringArray and its scene id mismatch check. Expected result: loadWorld throws descriptive errors for malformed content and returns scenes as SceneDef[].

loadWorld throws naming the missing file, such as s2.yaml, when a listed scene file is absent

technical_constraints: Missing scene error message must still contain '<sceneId>.yaml'

steps.action: Add three private helper functions above loadWorld, copied from world.ts L25-L43: isRecord(value), requireString(data, key, file), requireStringArray(data, key, file), each throwing Error with the messages `${file} missing string field: ${key}` and `${file} field must be a list of strings: ${key}`.
steps.code: function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> { return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value); }
steps.expected: File compiles with the three helpers available.

steps.action: Wrap fs.readFileSync in try/catch and throw new Error(`missing content file: ${file}`) on failure, so the message contains the file name such as s2.yaml.
steps.code: before: return parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')); -> after: let source: string; try { source = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'); } catch { throw new Error(`missing content file: ${file}`); } return parse(source);
steps.expected: Reading a nonexistent file throws an error containing the path.

steps.action: Rewrite the body: read world.yaml into raw, throw if !isRecord(raw), throw 'world.yaml field must be a list: characters' if raw.characters is not an array, build world: WorldDef via requireString for id, title, startScene and requireStringArray for scenes and flags. For each sceneId read scenes/<sceneId>.yaml, require isRecord, require id via requireString, throw `${relPath} declares id ${id}, expected ${sceneId}` on mismatch, push the record cast as SceneDef onto an array. Remove the existsSync check. Return { ...world, scenes } where scenes stays SceneDef[].
steps.code: const scenes: SceneDef[] = []; for (const sceneId of world.scenes) { const relPath = path.join('scenes', `${sceneId}.yaml`); const sceneRaw = readYaml(path.join(worldDir, relPath)); if (!isRecord(sceneRaw)) throw new Error(`${relPath} must be a YAML mapping`); const id = requireString(sceneRaw, 'id', relPath); if (id !== sceneId) throw new Error(`${relPath} declares id ${id}, expected ${sceneId}`); scenes.push(sceneRaw as unknown as SceneDef); }
steps.expected: loadWorld('content/worlds/the-boys-room') returns scenes array containing bedroom.
